title: Alzheimer’s pathology mediates arteriolosclerosis and cerebral amyloid angiopathy associations with cognition
title_zh: 阿尔茨海默病病理介导动脉硬化与脑淀粉样血管病与认知的关联
abstract: Abstract Vascular and neurodegenerative pathologies frequently co-occur in aging brains, yet the mechanisms linking vascular neuropathologies to cognitive impairment remain incompletely understood. We examined whether Alzheimer’s disease neuropathologic change (ADNC) and Lewy body disease (LBD) mediate or modify associations between vascular neuropathologies and domain-specific cognitive performance. The analytic sample included 1,269 decedents (mean age at death, 84.3 ± 9.1 years; 43.3% female; 94.7% White). At the last evaluation prior to death, 22.5% were cognitively normal, 2.4% were impaired but not mild cognitive impairment (MCI), 14.9% had MCI, and 60.2% had dementia. Vascular neuropathologies included arteriolosclerosis, atherosclerosis of the circle of Willis, cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA), gross infarcts/lacunes, and microinfarcts. Multivariable linear regression models evaluated associations with harmonized memory, executive function, and language z-scores adjusting for age at death, sex, education, and apolipoprotein E ε4 status. Effect modification by ADNC and LBD was tested. Mediation models estimated indirect and direct effects of vascular neuropathologies on cognition through ADNC or LBD using 5,000 bootstrap samples. Greater arteriolosclerosis severity was associated with worse memory (β=−0.16, 95% CI −0.23 to −0.09), executive function (β=−0.18, 95% CI −0.24 to −0.11), and language (β=−0.18, 95% CI −0.24 to −0.12; all p<0.001). CAA was strongly associated with poorer cognition across domains, including memory (β=−0.26, 95% CI −0.33 to −0.19; p<0.001). Atherosclerosis and infarcts showed more limited associations, while microinfarcts were not significantly associated with cognition. Mediation analyses indicated that ADNC statistically accounted for approximately 13–29% of the associations between arteriolosclerosis and cognition across domains and 64–91% of the associations between CAA and cognition. Direct effects of arteriolosclerosis remained significant, whereas CAA effects were largely explained by ADNC. Effect modification by ADNC and LBD was limited, although LBD attenuated associations of arteriolosclerosis and CAA with executive function. Mediation through LBD was not observed. This novel evidence shows that vascular neuropathologies influence cognition through defined pathways with statistically significant patterns of associations. In this autopsy-confirmed cohort, vascular neuropathologies showed different patterns of association with domain-specific cognitive performance and ADNC. A larger proportion of the association involving CAA was statistically accounted for by ADNC, whereas direct associations remained more apparent for arteriolosclerosis. This study clarifies how vascular and neurodegenerative processes interact to shape cognitive impact and inform mechanistic preventions.
abstract_zh: 摘要：血管与神经退行性病理在衰老大脑中经常共存，但血管神经病理与认知障碍之间的机制尚未完全阐明。我们研究了阿尔茨海默病神经病理改变（ADNC）和路易体病（LBD）是否介导或调节血管神经病理与特定认知领域表现之间的关联。分析样本包括1,269名已故者（死亡时平均年龄84.3±9.1岁；女性占43.3%；白人占94.7%）。在死亡前的最后一次评估中，22.5%认知正常，2.4%认知受损但未达到轻度认知障碍（MCI）标准，14.9%为MCI，60.2%为痴呆。血管神经病理包括小动脉硬化、威利斯环动脉粥样硬化、脑淀粉样血管病（CAA）、大面积梗塞/腔隙以及微梗塞。多变量线性回归模型评估了与记忆、执行功能和语言z分数的关联，并调整了死亡时年龄、性别、教育水平和载脂蛋白E ε4状态。还检验了ADNC和LBD的效应修饰。中介模型使用5,000次自助抽样估计血管神经病理通过ADNC或LBD对认知的间接和直接效应。更严重的小动脉硬化与记忆（β=−0.16，95% CI −0.23至−0.09）、执行功能（β=−0.18，95% CI −0.24至−0.11）和语言（β=−0.18，95% CI −0.24至−0.12）均显著相关（p<0.001）。CAA与各认知领域的下降高度相关，包括记忆（β=−0.26，95% CI −0.33至−0.19；p<0.001）。动脉粥样硬化和梗塞的关联更有限，微梗塞与认知无显著关联。中介分析显示，ADNC统计上解释了小动脉硬化与认知各领域关联的约13–29%，以及CAA与认知关联的64–91%。小动脉硬化的直接效应仍显著，而CAA的效应主要由ADNC解释。ADNC和LBD的效应修饰有限，尽管LBD减弱了小动脉硬化和CAA与执行功能的关联。未观察到通过LBD的中介。该新证据表明，血管神经病理通过已定义的路径影响认知，并呈现统计学显著的关联模式。在这组经尸检确认的队列中，血管神经病理与特定认知领域表现及ADNC呈现不同的关联模式。CAA相关的关联中，较大比例由ADNC统计解释，而小动脉硬化的直接关联更为明显。本研究阐明了血管与神经退行性过程如何相互作用，塑造认知影响，并为机制性预防提供信息。
